title: Nehanda Nyakasikana
summary: A spirit medium based in the Mazowe Valley of Mashonaland, Nehanda Nyakasikana is associated with the First Chimurenga (1896–1897) against the British South Africa Company. She was captured, tried over the killing of a colonial official and hanged in Salisbury, now Harare, on 27 April 1898. Her birth is placed around 1840. The pin marks Mazowe.

uncertainty.note: Birth is c. 1840 (Encyclopaedia Africana); the span covers the First Chimurenga to her execution.

as_recorded.value: executed by hanging on April 27, 1898, in Salisbury (now Harare)

where.modern_name: Mazowe, Mashonaland Central, Zimbabwe (pinned to the Mazowe Valley where she was based; she was executed in Harare)
where.historical_name: Mazowe Valley, Mashonaland, under British South Africa Company rule

importance.justification: Spirit medium associated with the 1896–97 uprising and remembered as a symbol of resistance.

reviewer_note: Pindula gives capture December 1897 and trial March 1898 but also contradicts itself on whether a trial occurred; Encyclopaedia Africana gives no capture date. Operational role in the uprising is described differently by sources; summary says only "associated with". Pin is Mazowe, execution site Harare.
